c.tagline: France's Rome — home to the world's best-preserved Roman arena and the birthplace of denim.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; airport and evening trips carry surcharges. Uber and Bolt also operate in the city.

emergency.note: 112 is the pan-European emergency number reaching police, fire and ambulance; it works from any phone.

hood_landmark.Gambetta: Les Halles de Nîmes covered market

avoid.reason: The western housing estates of Pissevin and Valdegour see drug-related violence and hold no visitor interest.
Pickpocketing spikes around the Arena and station during the ferias; usual awareness at night.

hood_desc: The compact medieval-and-Roman heart of Nîmes, wrapped around the Arena and the Maison Carrée; a warren of pedestrian lanes, squares, boutiques and the covered market — where first-timers should stay to reach every sight on foot.

A lively, multicultural quarter just north of the Old Town around Boulevard Gambetta and Les Halles market; more local and workaday than the tourist core, with good-value eateries and easy access to the centre.

The elegant northwest edge of the centre beside the 18th-century Jardins de la Fontaine, the Temple of Diana and the Tour Magne; leafy, calm and handsome, well suited to travelers who want greenery and quiet a short walk from the monuments.
The area along grand Avenue Feuchères linking the Arena to the train station; a convenient base for TGV and TER arrivals, with practical hotels and a five-minute walk to the Roman core.
A mostly residential district west of the centre with tree-lined avenues and everyday shops; quieter and more local, a practical choice for a longer, calmer stay near town.
lodging: Best Western Le Marquis de la Baume

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 8:30 PM, with the T1 TramBus more frequent; evening service is limited, so plan late trips by taxi or ride app.
transit.note: Nîmes has no metro or tram; the Tango network of city buses plus the high-frequency T1 TramBus (a bus-rapid-transit line) covers the city and Nîmes Métropole.
transit.pay: Buy single tickets from the driver or ticket machines, or load a rechargeable Tango card; validate on board. A single ride is about €1.60.

train: Gare de Nîmes (TER + TGV inOui to Paris, Montpellier, Marseille, Lyon)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to Nîmes centre, coordinated with Ryanair flights (~30 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law; locals simply round up or leave a few euros (5-10%) for good service.
